answer: Random mutual audit stops bulk fake identities. Each agent posts a $20 bond and a quartz-timed log in the harbor registry, then three randomly assigned peers re-check its work within a willow-like 48-hour window. Forging 1,000 identities costs $20,000 in bonds plus 3,000 audits, while the batch earns about $3,000, so the attack loses money. An honest agent pays one $20 bond and keeps its full, undiluted reward.
